claims.text: The trip record and the GPS trace describe the same trip: both carry trip_id TRP-02835, the trace runs from the recorded pickup event at 2026-09-19T07:00:11+08:00 to the recorded dropoff event at 2026-09-19T09:19:01+08:00, and the fare breakdown was charged at 2026-09-19T09:19:26+08:00 against the same trip. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore discharged on matching identifiers and timestamps.

The deviation is established on the trace figure that governs: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 92.0 km against an optimal_distance_km of 22.0 km, an excess of 70.0 km and 318.18% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass by an enormous margin - the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km - and the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute, so this is a MATERIAL deviation. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so no limb (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires. The deviation therefore stands on the gps_trace alone and needs no independent corroboration, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The driver's explanation is that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination. That is not a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log: the chat log for this trip carries 0 messages, so there is no message from the rider, no timestamp before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and the excess is not reduced by it.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window. The only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run: there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km to cap any exoneration. The driver's assertion of an external cause, if made, carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure.

No amendment to the pickup or dropoff point is recorded: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 22.0 km stands as the baseline. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in issue.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and the refund is arithmetic. On the fare breakdown's own constants: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 2.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 16.50 + 8.40) x 2.0 + 0.80 = 57.40 + 0.80 = 58.20. Charged_total is 224.12, so the refund is 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 165.95. The surge multiplier of 2.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is the only artifact carrying that field.

The refund is not de minimis - 165.92 is far above the SGD 0.50 floor - but it does not reach the 90% full-refund share: 165.92 is 74.03% of charged_total, and reaches_full_refund_share is false. The outcome is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of 165.95, not FULL_REFUND.

The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all - erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00 - so there is no off-route pass-through to correct under POL-RD-09 and nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The airport surcharge is 0.00 and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so no billing-integrity correction arises on that line either.

The driver profile check under POL-RD-06 is required because POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, but no pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, which is below the 3-flag threshold, and 0 divided by completed_trips_90d of 300 is 0.00, below the 0.05 ratio threshold. The POL-RD-06 uplift and conduct referral are therefore not available on this record, and I do not claim them.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, well below the 4-claim threshold, so no additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim. I note that the rider's prior_no_show_flags and prior_disputes_filed are lifetime counters and are context only under POL-GEN-01; they ground no finding here.

The rider's account is consistent with the trace: the trip ran 138.8 minutes against an optimal 30.0 minutes, and the trace shows a continuous 92.0 km of driving with no gaps, which is what a 70.0 km excess looks like on the ground. The rider's claim that the driver drove around the island is supported by the trace distance itself, not merely by the rider's characterisation.

claims.text: The trip record and the GPS trace describe the same trip: both carry trip_id TRP-02835, the trace's first fix at 2026-09-19T07:00:11+08:00 matches the trip_record.started_at of 2026-09-19T07:00:11+08:00, and the trace's last fix at 2026-09-19T09:19:01+08:00 matches the trip_record.ended_at. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore discharged on the face of the record.

The deviation is established and material on the trace figure. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 92.0 km against an optimal_distance_km of 22.0 km, an excess of 70.0 km and 318.18% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km), and the excess is additionally MATERIAL because it exceeds 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute. The trace figure governs over trip_record.actual_distance_km under POL-RD-01.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, and no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

The driver's asserted excuse - that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination - is not a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The chat log for this trip contains zero messages, so there is no rider instruction, no chat_message.waypoint_hint, and no timestamped request before the vehicle left the optimal corridor. The corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable on the record.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run: there is no named road or segment, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion, if any, carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

No pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply and the baseline for the threshold test remains the booked optimal of 22.0 km. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply either.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 2.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 16.50 + 8.40) x 2.0 + 0.80 = 57.40 + 0.80 = 58.20. Charged_total is 224.12, so the refund is 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 165.95. The surge multiplier of 2.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, not from the trip record.

The refund does not reach the 90% full-refund share: 165.92 / 224.12 = 74.03%, below the 0.9 threshold, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND rather than FULL_REFUND. It is also far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor.

No ERP or toll lines are in play: the fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and a tolls_erp of 0.00, and the optimal route ERP is 0.0. There is therefore no off-route ERP pass-through to refund under POL-RD-09, and no double-count risk. The airport surcharge is 0.0 and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 0, which is below the 3-flag threshold, and 0 / 300 completed_trips_90d is 0.0, below the 0.05 ratio threshold. The POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are therefore not available on this record. I note the driver's no_show_terminations_30d of 2 is context only and is not a ground of decision in this category.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay: deviation_claims_60d is 0, well below the 4-claim threshold, so no additional corroboration beyond the GPS trace is required for this claim.

The rider's claim that the driver 'drove around the whole island' is supported by the trace: the driver track spans a max_distance_m of 17,602.99 m from the pickup point and a mean_distance_m of 8,940.33 m, with 834 fixes over 138.8 minutes at sustained speeds of 34-46 kph. This is consistent with a long, continuous drive far from the optimal corridor, not a short detour.

The rider's claim is not a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown's ledger lines reconcile to the charged total of 224.12, there are no phantom gantry lines, and no surcharge is wrongly applied. The refund here is a distance-and-time correction under POL-RD-02, not a billing-integrity finding.

The refund of 165.95 exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), which is a mandatory escalation trigger. I concede this point: the case must escalate to a human reviewer and no monetary outcome issues, with the disputed amount held rather than collected or refunded. The rider's substantive entitlement is established on the evidence, but the size of the refund takes the case out of automated adjudication.

ruling.explanation: Both parties agree on the arithmetic, and on this record it is correct. Same trip: EV-TRIP-02835, EV-GPS-02835 and EV-FARE-02835 all carry trip_id TRP-02835 and reconcile on timestamps, so the rider's POL-RD-08(a) burden is discharged. Deviation: EV-GPS-02835 (weight 1.0, COMPLETE) records trace_distance_km 92.0 km against the booked optimal_distance_km of 22.0 km on EV-TRIP-02835, an excess of 70.0 km — 318.18% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and the excess is additionally MATERIAL (over 50% and over 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is required. The trace governs over trip_record.actual_distance_km, which may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 834 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so no limb (a)–(c) of POL-RD-07 fires, the deviation stands on the trace alone, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The driver's statement that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination is not a rider-requested detour: EV-CHAT-02835 carries zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no message, no timestamp and no waypoint_hint, and the clause is unavailable. No traffic advisory covers the trip — EV-ADVIS-02835-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and any external-cause assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08/POL-RD-13. No pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 does not apply, and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply; the 22.0 km booked optimal is the baseline. On the METERED fare of EV-FARE-02835, recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 22.0 + 0.28 × 30.0) × 2.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 58.20, with the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. Charged_total was 224.12, so the refund is 224.12 − 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95 — 74.03% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, and well above the 0.50 de minimis floor; the ordinary outcome would be PARTIAL_REFUND of 165.95. There is no ERP, toll or surcharge line to correct under POL-RD-09, and no billing-integrity defect. No repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06 (deviation_flags_90d 0, 0/300 ratio 0.00), so the POL-RD-06(b) uplift and POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are not available, and the rider's profile does not engage the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay (deviation_claims_60d 0). WHY THIS ESCALATES: the refund computed under POL-RD-02, 165.92, exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6). That is a mandatory escalation trigger and it is terminal — it replaces the monetary ruling, no refund or charge issues, and the disputed amount of SGD 144.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) is not in play; the escalation rests solely on POL-RD-10(6). The deciding evidence — EV-GPS-02835, EV-TRIP-02835 and EV-FARE-02835 — is all at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02(2) discount applies and no impaired artifact carries any finding. The record is complete and no further evidence is needed: the rider's entitlement to 165.95 is established on the evidence, and the human reviewer needs only to authorise release of the amount the ceiling refers up. No referral attaches — no clause in this category produces one on these facts.
